$comment: Per-building corrections to what the June 2010 LiDAR survey (behind the DataSF footprint heights) saw. Each entry sets exactly one of heightM (a roof height: a public record for a building completed after the survey, or, with placeholder: true, a stand-in plinth until a landmark model replaces the record; a placeholder keeps no storeys, use or units) and keepTower: true (the LiDAR tower stands although the spike check would drop it: a real steeple over a nave the roll counts as one storey; the build fails if no tower results). Pipeline config only: names here are provenance, never shipped into tiles. Keyed by sf16_bldgid; parcel is checked so a footprint id change fails the build loudly instead of silently mis-applying.

buildings.label: 415 Mission St tower
buildings.source: Completed 2018. Roof height 326 m (1,070 ft), public record (CTBUH Skyscraper Center). The footprint dataset reports a 0.24 m median height here: in June 2010 the site was the old Transbay Terminal ramps.

buildings.label: Sutro Tower upper structure (lattice, seen from above)
buildings.source: Placeholder until a landmark model replaces the sutro-tower probe's records. Sutro Tower is a 298 m open steel lattice on three legs (public record); the footprint dataset outlines its upper structure as seen from above, and the LiDAR fills that outline as a solid prism (median 210.4 m, max 286.4 m over 683 m²). A 3 m plinth marks the footprint instead of a 231 m solid block.

buildings.label: Mission Dolores Basilica bell tower
buildings.source: The basilica beside the old mission chapel (parcel 3566001, built 1913 per the 2025 roll) has bell towers over its front; the LiDAR max over the footprint is 39.0 m above a 14.1 m median, a tower the moment model accepts (about 55 m², rising 3.4 times its width). The roll lists 1 storey (the nave is one tall room), so the spike check reads the tower as a LiDAR spike. Kept: the LiDAR is the evidence, the storey count is not.
